expl.summary: The formula places every jet on 16 neurons. Each neuron is an intercept plus a sum of if-statements on jet observables (and a few linear terms), clipped at zero; in this one-term version of formula 690 each observable appears in at most one term per neuron, and the formula was then re-tuned on the network's predictions. Each class score adds some neurons and subtracts others, and the largest score decides the class; the formula classifies 80.8% of validation jets correctly. The g score rests on particle multiplicity (neuron 1: many particles, high −Σz ln z and ln ΣpT, +47%, the neuron whose freezing costs the most accuracy, 11.8 points), from which the q score subtracts (-23%). Both light-parton scores subtract the neuron that is on for jet mass above 74.3 GeV with few particles and low D₂ (neuron 4: -29.5% of the q score, -15% of the g score) and add the low-mass neuron (neuron 9: m(50 hardest) below 71.7 GeV, +25% and +14%); the q score follows D₂(β=2) and τ₂₁(β=2) (rank correlations 0.681 and 0.659), the g score N₂ (0.698). The W and Z scores both subtract the large-λ₁+λ₂ neuron that is on above 64.1 GeV of jet mass (neuron 8, -24% and -25%) and add the neuron for ΣpT(50 hardest) above 935 GeV with few particles (neuron 5, +16% and +18%). They are split by jet mass (the mass of the 64 particles seen): the neuron that is pushed down above 87.4 GeV (neuron 0) raises the W score (+10%) and lowers the Z score (-18%), the below-100-GeV neuron with small e₂ (neuron 11) raises the W score (+12%), and the neuron for mass above 87.4 GeV with m_SD below 97.1 GeV (neuron 7) raises the Z score (+8.9%) and lowers the W score (-6.3%). The t score subtracts a ΣpT(20 hardest) neuron that is switched off above 161 GeV of mass, twice the W mass (neuron 13, -36%), and adds the large-ΣzΔR and τ₁ neuron (neuron 10, +27%); it rises with ΣzΔR (0.722) and τ₁ (0.721).
